The key changes are:
1. `/health`: change the initial response from 503 to 200 and the body to `{"status":"ok"}`.
2. `/users`: use a parameterized `name` string in the SQL query instead of concatenating it with the input value, so user input is never executed as SQL.

## Explanation of changes

**`/health` (line 8, 9):** The initial response is now returned successfully (`200`) with the JSON body `{"status":"ok"}` instead of a 503 starting status.

**`/users` (lines 10-12):** The query is changed from `select name from users where name = '` + `name`` + `'` to a parameterized query `select name from users where name = ?` with the single `name` value as a parameter. This guarantees the input value is never interpolated into SQL, so an injected string returns no rows and yields an empty list rather than a SQL error.

## Implementation

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        url=urlparse(self.path)
        if url.path=='/health':
            self.send_response(200);body={'status':'ok'}
        elif url.path=='/users':
            db=sqlite3.connect(':memory:');db.execute('create table users(name text)');db.executemany('insert into users values (?)',[('Alice',),('Bob',)])
            name=parse_qs(url.query).get('name',[''])[0]
            body=[r[0] for r in db.execute("select name from users where name = ?",[name])]
            db.close();self.send_response(200)
        else:self.send_response(404);body={}
        data=json.dumps(body).encode();self.send_header('Content-Type','application/json');self.send_header('Content-Length',str(len(data)));self.end_headers();self.wfile.write(data)
